result.narrative: Larsen & Toubro sits in the Watch band at a score of 28.4 (PD 0.1837), driven almost entirely by a single severity-3 news item rather than by payment behaviour, which is itself mild. The one open overdue on record is INR 18M at 12 days past due against a large INR 350M whole-turnover limit on 90-day terms, and the only prior notification on file resolved just 6 days late, so there is no pattern of deterioration in the payment leg. The band is being held up by a news story reporting that a Karnataka state minister has asked officials to blacklist L&T over project delays - a severity-3 regulatory_action headline (raw 58.8, weighted 20.6 of the 28.4 total score) that is not corroborated by any other outlet and describes a request, not a confirmed blacklisting or contract loss. All other recent coverage (large new orders, stock rallies, analyst upgrades) is neutral-to-positive and scored zero severity. The recommended action is to maintain the current limit of INR 350,000,000 with no change, as the probability of default remains within appetite; the adjudicator agreed with this outcome but added caveats, flagging that the Watch score rests on thin, single-source, non-final news and that the current overdue, while small, is still open and worth confirming resolves promptly. To move to a lower band the buyer would need the overdue to clear cleanly and the regulatory story to fade or be shown as unfounded; conversely, an actual blacklist order, a confirmed contract cancellation, or payment slippage toward roughly 38 days past due would push the score toward the High Risk threshold.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the existing INR 350,000,000 limit; the Watch band is driven almost entirely by a single, uncorroborated regulatory-action headline rather than by payment deterioration, and the adjudicator agreed with caveats flagging that thin evidence base for monitoring.
